result:
**How the de-duplication was reworked**

The collapse happens in the results viewer's `filter-context.tsx`, which builds the table and timeline from `/obstree`. The `/obstree` backend returns the same orderable concept under several branches, each carrying a copy of the same obs list.

- **PR #3345 (commit `16600fb`)** first keyed de-duplication on `conceptUuid` instead of `flatName`. That collapsed a concept that legitimately appears under two panels (Platelets under Hematology and Bloodwork) into one row. A follow-up commit in the same PR scoped the key to the rendered panel group.
- **PR #3374 (commit `d47d346`)** replaced that key with a normalized-branch step. Branches are identified by panel group key plus concept UUID. Duplicate branches merge their obs with a multiset-max union, so copied lists collapse, while two equal obs inside one list (two genuinely separate results with the same value and time) stay as two rows. Tests cover the 1-row, 1-row-across-Bloodwork, and 2-row cases, and the header count follows the rendered rows.

**Server-side change for telling copies apart**

I could not find the ticket. None of the commit messages I searched in the chart, `openmrs-module-webservices.rest` or `openmrs-core` name it, and the PR bodies are not reachable through these tools. What I can confirm is the gap it would close: `ObsTreeResource1_9.getObsMap` emits each obs as only `value`, `obsDatetime`, `interpretation` and reference-range fields, with no obs UUID. A client therefore cannot tell two identical obs apart from one obs repeated across branches. The ticket most likely proposes adding an obs UUID to that payload, but I have not verified that, so I have left it out of the array.

A form could happily accept a value the backend then rejects.\n\nThe wrapper now fetches the ranges for the concepts of all numeric\nquestions from /conceptreferencerange before the form is built, and\nnarrows each question to the absolute bounds of the range that applies to\nthe patient. A bound already set by the schema is never widened, the\nstricter of the two wins. Only the absolute bounds are used, which is what\nthe backend validates against too.\n\nIf the ranges cannot be fetched (older backends do not have the resource,\nand there is nothing to fetch while offline) the form loads unconstrained,\nexactly as before.\n\n* (fix) O3-5850: Page and bound the concept reference range request\n\nTwo problems with fetching every concept in one unbounded request.\n\nThe resource is paged, and REST defaults to 50 results, so a form with\nmore than 50 numeric concepts silently lost the ranges of everything past\nthe first page. A NEW order plus its\nauto-generated DISCONTINUE order made the same result show twice; two orders,\nfour times, and so on.\n\nRoot cause\nThe /obstree backend returns the same orderable-test concept under several\nbranches of the orderable-tests tree (effectively one branch per order), each\nbranch carrying the same single observation. In filter-context's tableData\nbuilder the de-duplication key is based on test.flatName, which differs per\nbranch, so the identical observation is not collapsed and renders once per\nbranch.\n\nFix\nKey the de-duplication on the observation's conceptUuid instead of flatName.\nThe same observation (same concept + datetime + value) reached via different\nbranches now collapses to a single row, while genuinely different tests stay\nseparate. One-line change, no new dependencies, no new i18n keys.\n\n* (fix) Scope lab results dedupe to the rendered panel, not just conceptUuid\n\nKeying de-duplication on conceptUuid alone collapsed the same observation\nacross different rendered panels. A concept mounted under two roots (e.g.\nPlatelets under both Hematology and Bloodwork) was deduped to a single row,\ndropping the tree view from 3 tables to 2 and Platelets from 2 rows to 1.\n\nScope the dedupe key to the panel group key derived from flatName, so the\nsame concept that legitimately appears under different panels stays as\nseparate rows while true duplicates within one panel still collapse. Extract\nthe group-key derivation into a shared helper used by both the dedupe and the\ngrouping step so the two scopes stay aligned.\n\nAdd regression tests covering both directions: collapse within one panel and\nkeep across two panels.\n\n\nCo-authored-by: NethmiRodrigo <nethmi.dilinika@gmail.com>","ticketKeys":[],"pullRequests":[3345],"linksSource":"message, unverified"},{"repo":"github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-patient-chart","hash":"3568fa685f2d33a17b6fb975b089ed4b0abb5cfe","date":"2026-05-17T21:37:59.000Z","author":"denniskigen","subject":"fix: prevent escaped condition duplicate warnings","message":"fix: prevent escaped condition duplicate warnings","ticketKeys":[],"pullRequests":[],"linksSource":"message, unverified"},{"repo":"github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-patient-chart","hash":"e8a91dc03fb49a124935db66973019874361c307","date":"2026-05-15T18:35:22.000Z","author":"Dennis Kigen","subject":"(test) Port task-list tests from openmrs-esm-task-list#9 (#3303)","message":"(test) Port task-list tests from openmrs-esm-task-list#9 (#3303)\n\n* (test) Port task-list tests from openmrs-esm-task-list#9\n\nSalvages the test work from @pirupius's PR\nopenmrs/openmrs-esm-task-list#9 before the standalone repo is archived\n(its source was forked into packages/esm-patient-task-list-app).\n\nUnit tests\n----------\nAdds the gap-filling test cases from pirupius's three test files to the\nexisting patient-chart equivalents. If a later one failed, the results were already\nsaved, the order was not COMPLETED, and the form stayed in create mode.\nRetrying posted the obs to the encounter again. If the fulfiller update\nwas the one that failed, every retry added another copy and then failed\non the discontinue, because the backend rejects stopping an order twice.\n\nWhen an order already has saved results but is not COMPLETED, the form\nnow fills in the saved values and saving updates those obs. It then\ndiscontinues the order only if it is still active and marks it as\nfulfilled. After a failed attempt, the form refetches its results in the\nbackground, and Save is available again before that refetch finishes.\nA quick retry in that window used to take the create path again. If the\nfetch fails, nothing is saved.\n\n* Keep the user's edits when saved results load\n\nOnly fill in saved result values for fields the user hasn't changed.\nAfter a failed save, the form refetches the saved results, and if the\nuser corrected a value while that was in flight, the refetched value\nreplaced their correction.\n\n* test: verify lab result edits are saved after delayed refresh\n\nExtend the delayed-results regression test through Save and close. A form could happily accept a value the backend then rejects.\n\nThe wrapper now fetches the ranges for the concepts of all numeric\nquestions from /conceptreferencerange before the form is built, and\nnarrows each question to the absolute bounds of the range that applies to\nthe patient. A bound already set by the schema is never widened, the\nstricter of the two wins. Only the absolute bounds are used, which is what\nthe backend validates against too.\n\nIf the ranges cannot be fetched (older backends do not have the resource,\nand there is nothing to fetch while offline) the form loads unconstrained,\nexactly as before.\n\n* (fix) O3-5850: Page and bound the concept reference range request\n\nTwo problems with fetching every concept in one unbounded request.\n\nThe resource is paged, and REST defaults to 50 results, so a form with\nmore than 50 numeric concepts silently lost the ranges of everything past\nthe first page. Each request now follows its next link until the backend\nruns out of pages.\n\nA single concept the backend cannot resolve also used to take the whole\nform down with it, since catchError turned any failure into an empty map.\nConcepts are now resolved and deduplicated against the schema's\nconceptReferences before the request, so references known not to resolve\nare never sent, and the remainder goes out in bounded batches. A batch\nthat still fails costs only its own ranges.\n\n* Update packages/esm-form-entry-app/src/app/form-schema/concept-reference-ranges.ts\n\nCo-authored-by: Dennis Kigen <kigen.work@gmail.com>\n\n* Update packages/esm-form-entry-app/src/app/form-schema/concept-refer","messageCut":"message cut to 2000 characters","ticketKeys":["O3-5850"],"pullRequests":[3546],"linksSource":"message, unverified"},{"repo":"github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-patient-chart","hash":"1a2af778aa7f86ea2c1fc944e46d6a7548af2f88","date":"2026-07-21T19:50:58.000Z","author":"Dennis Kigen","subject":"(fix) O3-5822: Dedupe diagnoses in visit-level rollups (#3496)","message":"(fix) O3-5822: Dedupe diagnoses in visit-level rollups (#3496)","ticketKeys":["O3-5822"],"pullRequests":[3496],"linksSource":"message, unverified"},{"repo":"github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-patient-chart","hash":"d47d346cc105c4c72dfb1ce68a05abbcb1ad4f84","date":"2026-06-10T12:22:43.000Z","author":"Dennis Kigen","subject":"(fix) Deduplicate overlapping test result branches in the results viewer (#3374)","message":"(fix) Deduplicate overlapping test result branches in the results viewer (#3374)","ticketKeys":[],"pullRequests":[3374],"linksSource":"message, unverified"},{"repo":"github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-patient-chart","hash":"16600fbfd85e41b98eaaa84817293a6b9e2af65f","date":"2026-06-10T06:24:55.000Z","author":"cerveaubleu64","subject":"(fix) De-duplicate repeated lab results in the test results viewer (#3345)","message":"(fix) De-duplicate repeated lab results in the test results viewer (#3345)\n\n* (fix) Tests results: dedupe lab results by conceptUuid to stop duplicate rows\n\nProblem\nOn the patient-chart lab results viewer, a single lab result is rendered\nmultiple times — once per order placed for that test. A NEW order plus its\nauto-generated DISCONTINUE order made the same result show twice; two orders,\nfour times, and so on.\n\nRoot cause\nThe /obstree backend returns the same orderable-test concept under several\nbranches of the orderable-tests tree (effectively one branch per order), each\nbranch carrying the same single observation. In filter-context's tableData\nbuilder the de-duplication key is based on test.flatName, which differs per\nbranch, so the identical observation is not collapsed and renders once per\nbranch.\n\nFix\nKey the de-duplication on the observation's conceptUuid instead of flatName.\nThe same observation (same concept + datetime + value) reached via different\nbranches now collapses to a single row, while genuinely different tests stay\nseparate. One-line change, no new dependencies, no new i18n keys.\n\n* (fix) Scope lab results dedupe to the rendered panel, not just conceptUuid\n\nKeying de-duplication on conceptUuid alone collapsed the same observation\nacross different rendered panels. A concept mounted under two roots (e.g.\nPlatelets under both Hematology and Bloodwork) was deduped to a single row,\ndropping the tree view from 3 tables to 2 and Platelets from 2 rows to 1.\n\nScope the dedupe key to the panel group key derived from flatName, so the\nsame concept that legitimately appears under different panels stays as\nseparate rows while true duplicates within one panel still collapse. Extract\nthe group-key derivation into a shared helper used by both the dedupe and the\ngrouping step so the two scopes stay aligned.\n\nAdd regression tests covering both directions: collapse within one panel and\nkeep across two panels.\n\n\nCo-authored-by: NethmiRodrigo <nethmi.dilinika@gmail.com>","ticketKeys":[],"pullRequests":[3345],"linksSource":"message, unverified"},{"repo":"github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-patient-chart","hash":"3568fa685f2d33a17b6fb975b089ed4b0abb5cfe","date":"2026-05-17T21:37:59.000Z","author":"denniskigen","subject":"fix: prevent escaped condition duplicate warnings","message":"fix: prevent escaped condition duplicate warnings","ticketKeys":[],"pullRequests":[],"linksSource":"message, unverified"},{"repo":"github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-patient-chart","hash":"e8a91dc03fb49a124935db66973019874361c307","date":"2026-05-15T18:35:22.000Z","author":"Dennis Kigen","subject":"(test) Port task-list tests from openmrs-esm-task-list#9 (#3303)","message":"(test) Port task-list tests from openmrs-esm-task-list#9 (#3303)\n\n* (test) Port task-list tests from openmrs-esm-task-list#9\n\nSalvages the test work from @pirupius's PR\nopenmrs/openmrs-esm-task-list#9 before the standalone repo is archived\n(its source was forked into packages/esm-patient-task-list-app).\n\nUnit tests\n----------\nAdds the gap-filling test cases from pirupius's three test files to the\nexisting patient-chart equivalents. The backend saves inline\norders inside the same transaction as the obs, so a failed discontinue\nno longer leaves the results saved behind it.\n\nPreviously the results, the discontinue and the fulfiller update were\nthree separate requests. If a later one failed, the results were already\nsaved, the order was not COMPLETED, and the form stayed in create mode.\nRetrying posted the obs to the encounter again. If the fulfiller update\nwas the one that failed, every retry added another copy and then failed\non the discontinue, because the backend rejects stopping an order twice.\n\nWhen an order already has saved results but is not COMPLETED, the form\nnow fills in the saved values and saving updates those obs. A NEW order plus its\nauto-generated DISCONTINUE order made the same result show twice; two orders,\nfour times, and so on.\n\nRoot cause\nThe /obstree backend returns the same orderable-test concept under several\nbranches of the orderable-tests tree (effectively one branch per order), each\nbranch carrying the same single observation. In filter-context's tableData\nbuilder the de-duplication key is based on test.flatName, which differs per\nbranch, so the identical observation is not collapsed and renders once per\nbranch.\n\nFix\nKey the de-duplication on the observation's conceptUuid instead of flatName.\nThe same observation (same concept + datetime + value) reached via different\nbranches now collapses to a single row, while genuinely different tests stay\nseparate. One-line change, no new dependencies, no new i18n keys.\n\n* (fix) Scope lab results dedupe to the rendered panel, not just conceptUuid\n\nKeying de-duplication on conceptUuid alone collapsed the same observation\nacross different rendered panels. A concept mounted under two roots (e.g.\nPlatelets under both Hematology and Bloodwork) was deduped to a single row,\ndropping the tree view from 3 tables to 2 and Platelets from 2 rows to 1.\n\nScope the dedupe key to the panel group key derived from flatName, so the\nsame concept that legitimately appears under different panels stays as\nseparate rows while true duplicates within one panel still collapse. Extract\nthe group-key derivation into a shared helper used by both the dedupe and the\ngrouping step so the two scopes stay aligned.\n\nAdd regression tests covering both directions: collapse within one panel and\nkeep across two panels.\n\n\nCo-authored-by: NethmiRodrigo <nethmi.dilinika@gmail.com>","ticketKeys":[],"pullRequests":[3345],"linksSource":"message, In filter-context's tableData\nbuilder the de-duplication key is based on test.flatName, which differs per\nbranch, so the identical observation is not collapsed and renders once per\nbranch.\n\nFix\nKey the de-duplication on the observation's conceptUuid instead of flatName.\nThe same observation (same concept + datetime + value) reached via different\nbranches now collapses to a single row, while genuinely different tests stay\nseparate. A concept mounted under two roots (e.g.\nPlatelets under both Hematology and Bloodwork) was deduped to a single row,\ndropping the tree view from 3 tables to 2 and Platelets from 2 rows to 1.\n\nScope the dedupe key to the panel group key derived from flatName, so the\nsame concept that legitimately appears under different panels stays as\nseparate rows while true duplicates within one panel still collapse. A NEW order plus its\nauto-generated DISCONTINUE order made the same result show twice; two orders,\nfour times, and so on.\n\nRoot cause\nThe /obstree backend returns the same orderable-test concept under several\nbranches of the orderable-tests tree (effectively one branch per order), each\nbranch carrying the same single observation. In filter-context's tableData\nbuilder the de-duplication key is based on test.flatName, which differs per\nbranch, so the identical observation is not collapsed and renders once per\nbranch.\n\nFix\nKey the de-duplication on the observation's conceptUuid instead of flatName.\nThe same observation (same concept + datetime + value) reached via different\nbranches now collapses to a single row, while genuinely different tests stay\nseparate. One-line change, no new dependencies, no new i18n keys.\n\n* (fix) Scope lab results dedupe to the rendered panel, not just conceptUuid\n\nKeying de-duplication on conceptUuid alone collapsed the same observation\nacross different rendered panels. A concept mounted under two roots (e.g.\nPlatelets under both Hematology and Bloodwork) was deduped to a single row,\ndropping the tree view from 3 tables to 2 and Platelets from 2 rows to 1.\n\nScope the dedupe key to the panel group key derived from flatName, so the\nsame concept that legitimately appears under different panels stays as\nseparate rows while true duplicates within one panel still collapse. Extract\nthe group-key derivation into a shared helper used by both the dedupe and the\ngrouping step so the two scopes stay aligned.\n\nAdd regression tests covering both directions: collapse within one panel and\nkeep across two panels.\n\n\nCo-authored-by: NethmiRodrigo 112: 		
113: 		ObsService obsService = Context.getObsService();
114: 		ConceptService conceptService = Context.getConceptService();
115: 		List<Person> whom = Arrays.asList((Person)patient);

118: 		if (concept.getSet()) {

128: 	private List<Map<String, Object>> getSetMembers(List<Person> whom, Collection<ConceptSet> conceptSets, 
129: 			Date fromDate, Date toDate, ObsService obsService, ConceptService conceptService) {
130: 		
131: 		List<Map<String, Object>> mapList = new ArrayList<Map<String, Object>>();
132: 		
133: 		if (conceptSets == null || conceptSets.isEmpty()) {
134: 			return mapList;
135: 		}
136: 		
137: 		for (ConceptSet conceptSet : conceptSets) {

139: 			if (concept.getSet()) {

142: 			}
143: 			else {
144: 				mapList.add(getObsMap(whom, concept, fromDate, toDate, obsService, conceptService));

146: 		}

148: 		return mapList;
